paper.title: On the Suboptimality of Thompson Sampling in High Dimensions

settings.name_in_paper: Linear combinatorial semi-bandit over the set of two disjoint paths X^p (Bernoulli rewards)
unmapped: Action set consists of exactly two disjoint decisions (1,...,1,0,...,0) and (0,...,0,1,...,1) of size m = d/2
settings.definition_quote: We define $\cX^{p}$ the set of paths of the directed acyclic graph depicted in figure... This set has two disjoint decisions $(1,...,1,0,...,0)$ and $(0,...,0,1,...,1)$ of equal size $m = {d \over 2}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Non-linear combinatorial semi-bandit with X = {sum_{i<=m} e_i, e_{m+1}} and product reward (Bernoulli)
unmapped: Known non-linear reward function f: product of the m base-arm parameters for the first decision, constant 1-Delta for the second
The learner knows the reward function f
settings.definition_quote: Consider a non-linear combinatorial bandit problem over combinatorial set $\cX = \left\{ \sum_{i=1}^{m} e_i , e_{m+1} \right\}$ ... reward function $f(x,\theta) = \prod_{i=1}^{m} \theta_i$ if $x = \sum_{i=1}^{m} e_i$ and $f(x,\theta) = 1 - \Delta$ otherwise.

source.label: th:linear_frequentist
source.quote: Consider a linear combinatorial bandit problem over combinatorial set $\cX^{p}$ and parameter $\theta_i = 1$ if $1 \le i \le d/2$ and $\theta_i = 1 - {\Delta \over m}$ otherwise. Assume that ${\Delta \over m}+{1\over \sqrt{m}} < {1\over2}$. Then the regret of TS is lower bounded by R(T,\theta) \ge {\Delta \over 4 p_\Delta}(1 - (1-p_{\Delta})^{T-1})...

results.notes: Lower bound for the specific algorithm TS on a specific instance; Delta is the gap between the two decisions.

bound.expression: Delta/(4*p_Delta)*(1 - (1 - p_Delta)**(T_0 - 1)) + C_3*Delta*((1 - g_Delta)**T_0 - (1 - g_Delta)**(T - T_0 + 1))/g_Delta

conditions: specific algorithm: Thompson Sampling with uniform prior
instance theta_i = 1 for i <= d/2 and theta_i = 1 - Delta/m otherwise
Delta <= 1/6

source.label: th:linear_frequentist_bis
source.quote: Then there exists universal constants $C_2,C_3$ such that for all $T \ge T_0(m) \equiv C_2 m^2\ln m$, and $\Delta \le 1/6$ and $m \geq 5$, the regret of TS is lower bounded by R(T,\theta) \ge \frac{\Delta}{4p_\Delta}(1- (1-p_\Delta)^{T_0-1}) + C_3 \Delta \frac{(1- g_\Delta)^{T_0}-(1-g_\Delta)^{T-T_0+1}}{g_\Delta} with g_\Delta = {(2\Delta)^m \over m!}...

results.notes: Small-gap regime lower bound for TS.

conditions: specific algorithm: Thompson Sampling with uniform prior
maximum over theta in [0,1]^d

source.label: co:linear_minimax
source.quote: Consider a linear combinatorial bandit problem over combinatorial set $\cX^{p}$ with $m \geq 5$. If $T > 2^mm!$ then the minimax regret of TS is lower bounded by \max_{\theta \in [0,1]^d} R(T,\theta) \ge C_4 m T^{1 - {2 \over d}}

results.notes: C_4 universal constant. Proof uses threshold 3^m m! but statement says 2^m m!; recorded as stated. 2/d = 1/m.

conditions: specific algorithm: Thompson Sampling with uniform prior
maximum over theta in [0,1]^d

results.notes: Linear minimax regret for TS when T is below the threshold.

conditions: action set is X^p (two disjoint paths)

source.label: co:linear_minimax
source.quote: The minimax regret of ESCB for this set $\cX^p$ is upper bounded by: \max_{\theta \in [0,1]^d} R(T,\theta) \le C_5 d^{1 \over 4} \sqrt{ T \ln T}. with $C_5 \ge 0$ a universal constant.

results.notes: Derived from known ESCB analysis (Degenne & Perchet / Cuvelier et al.); no proof given in the paper. Horizon knowledge not stated.

results.notes: Lower bound for TS with forced exploration.

source.quote: Then if $T>4^m m!$ and $T > T_0(m,l) \equiv C_6 m^2 (\ln m)\ell^{1 \over {1 \over 4} - {1 \over m}}$ the minimax regret of TS with $\ell$ forced exploration rounds is lower bounded by \max_{\theta \in [0,1]^d} R(T,\theta) \ge C_7 C(\ell,m) {m\over \ell} T^{1 - {1 \over m}}.

results.notes: C_6, C_7 universal constants. The proof writes the result with O(.) notation, which is a typo for Omega.

source.label: cor:nonlinear_minimax
source.quote: Consider ${\cal F}$ the class of $1$-Lipschitz functions. The minimax regret of TS is lower bounded by: \max_{\theta \in [0,1]^d, f \in {\cal F}} R(T,\theta,f) \ge C_1 T^{1 - {1 \over d}}, with $C_1 > 0$ a universal constant

results.notes: Obtained by setting Delta = T^{-1/d} in Theorem 6. The maximum is taken over general 1-Lipschitz f, so the setting is broader than s2's fixed product reward. The CUCB upper bound in the same corollary is recorded in cited_results.
